observations: Photo 0 shows two square tiles with a white background and grey/gold marble-style veining on a display rack.
Photo 1 shows two square tiles with a black background and gold/silver swirling patterns on a display rack.
Photo 2 shows a single white and gold veined tile leaning against a wall on a dirt floor.
High-gloss reflections are visible on the surface of the black tiles in photo 1.
The watermark 'CUBATEC LUX HOMES' appears on all three photos.
No manufacturer boxes or the back of the tiles are visible.

claims.evidence: Quality of tile (wear rating, water absorption) cannot be determined from photos.
photo 1 shows clear reflections of the photographer and surroundings on the tile surface.
The tiles appear square, but no measuring tape or scale is provided to confirm the 60cm x 60cm dimensions.

risks.risk: The tiles may be ceramic rather than more durable and expensive porcelain.
risks.proof: A photo of the side profile or the unglazed back of the tile.

risks.risk: The tiles may be unbranded or from a low-tier manufacturer.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's box showing the brand and grade.

risks.risk: Edges may be chipped or the surface scratched, which is common in loose tile storage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the corners and edges of the actual stock being sold.
risks.if_unproven: priced as Grade B or seconds

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturer's box showing brand, material (porcelain/ceramic), and grade.
Photo of the back of a tile.
Photo of a tile with a measuring tape across it to confirm 60x60cm size.
Confirmation of the total quantity available in the same batch/lot.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as polished floor tiles. They can be priced at the worst-case scenario (generic ceramic) until further proof of material or brand is provided.
